extracted.intended_audience: applicants, licensees, and their counsel/representatives in Wireless Radio Services; FCC staff and practitioners handling FCC filings
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules and criteria governing what counts as major/minor modifications, STA requests, public notices, defective/dismissed applications, petitions to deny, license grants, hearings, and construction/coverage obligations in Wireless Radio Services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major modifications for microwave/aural/television broadcast auxiliary services
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as specified in paragraphs (d)(2) and (d)(3), the following are major actions (in addition to filings in paragraph (a)) for stations licensed to provide fixed point-to-point, point-to-multipoint, or multipoint-to-point communications on a site-specific basis, or fixed or mobile communications on an area-specific basis under part 101:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any change in transmit antenna location by more than 5 seconds in latitude or longitude for fixed point-to-point facilities; any change in coordinates of the center of operation or increase in radius of a circular area of operation, or expansion in latitude/longitude limits of a rectangular area, or any change in any other kind of area operation; any increase in frequency tolerance; any increase in bandwidth; any change in emission type; any increase in EIRP greater than 3 dB; any increase in transmit antenna height (AMSL) more than 3 meters (except as specified in paragraph (d)(3)); any increase in transmit antenna beamwidth (except as specified in (d)(3)); any change in transmit antenna polarization; any change in transmit antenna azimuth greater than 1 degree (except as specified in (d)(3)); and any change which together with all minor modifications or amendments since the last major modification produces a cumulative effect exceeding any of the above major criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAS/DEMS transmit antenna location exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to transmit antenna location of Multiple Address System (MAS) Remote Units and Digital Electronic Message Service (DEMS) User Units are not major.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit exception to the major-action list for microwave/auxiliary services; see paragraph (d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-major status for certain MAS/DEMS path changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in accordance with paragraphs (d)(1)(vi), (d)(1)(vii) and (d)(1)(ix) are not major for specified MAS/DEMS systems and path types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to listed systems/path types (e.g., Fixed Two-Way MAS remote-to-master, Fixed One-Way Inbound MAS remote-to-master, Multiple Two-Way MAS remote-to-master and master-to-remote, Multiple One-Way Outbound MAS master-to-remote, Mobile MAS Master, Fixed Two-Way DEMS user-to-nodal, Multiple Two-Way DEMS nodal-to-user and user-to-nodal). Note: for these systems the data provided by applicants is either a typical value for a parameter or a fixed value given in the Form instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major actions for Air-ground Radiotelephone Service
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to paragraph (a) filings, the following are major actions applying to stations licensed to provide service in the Air-ground Radiotelephone Service:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request an authorization to relocate an existing General Aviation ground station; or request the first authorization for a new Commercial Aviation ground station at locations other than those listed in §22.859 of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major changes for industrial radiopositioning, Maritime and Aviation services (except Maritime Public Coast VHF)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to paragraph (a) changes, the following are major changes for stations licensed in industrial radiopositioning stations (exclusive frequencies), Maritime and Aviation services (except Maritime Public Coast VHF):
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any change in antenna azimuth; any change in beamwidth; any change in antenna location; any change in emission type; any increase in antenna height; any increase in authorized power; any increase in emission bandwidth.

rubrics_metrics.name: International coordination requirement makes change major in Maritime Public Coast VHF (CMRS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change requiring international coordination in the Maritime Public Coast VHF (CMRS) Service is major.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit major-category for changes that trigger international coordination obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major changes for ship stations
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to paragraph (a) changes, the following are major for ship stations:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request for additional equipment; a change in ship category; a request for assignment of a Maritime Mobile Service Identity (MMSI) number; or a request to increase the number of ships on an existing fleet license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major changes for aircraft stations
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to paragraph (a) changes, the following are major for aircraft stations:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request to increase the number of aircraft on an existing fleet license; or a request to change the type of aircraft (private or air carrier).

rubrics_metrics.name: Major changes for amateur licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to paragraph (a) changes, the following are major for amateur licenses:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An upgrade of an existing license; or a change of call sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default minor changes and illustrative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change not specifically listed above as major is considered minor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: any pro forma assignment or transfer of control; any name change not involving change in ownership or control; any email or physical mailing address and/or telephone number changes; changes in contact person; change to vessel name on a ship station license; change to a site-specific license (except certain PLMRS or part 101 licenses) where interference contours are not extended and co-channel separation criteria are met; conversion of multiple site-specific licenses into a single wide-area license where there is no change in composite interference contour or service area.

rubrics_metrics.name: STA filing requirements for Wireless Telecommunications Services
rubrics_metrics.description: Carriers may request Special Temporary Authority (STA) to operate new or modified equipment; such requests must be filed electronically using FCC Form 601 and must contain complete details about the proposed operation and the circumstances that fully justify and necessitate the grant of STA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be filed at least 10 days prior to proposed operation or 10 days before expiration when seeking extension. Late-filed requests (<10 days) may be expedited only if compelling reasons are given. Requests for STA for Contraband Interdiction System operations will be afforded expedited consideration if filed at least one day prior. Requests must be accompanied by the proper filing fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: When STA may be granted without Public Notice
rubrics_metrics.description: STA may be granted without being listed in a Public Notice, or prior to 30 days after such listing, if one of several criteria is met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include: STA valid ≤30 days with no plan to file for regular authorization; STA valid ≤60 days pending filing for regular authorization; STA to allow interim operation to facilitate completion of authorized construction or to provide substantially same service as previously authorized; finding of extraordinary circumstances requiring operation in the public interest where delay would seriously prejudice the public interest; STA for Contraband Interdiction System operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: STA term limits and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may grant STA for up to 180 days under section 309(f) when extraordinary circumstances require, and may grant extensions of 180 days if the applicant shows extraordinary circumstances warrant an extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 180-day grants/extensions are exceptional and tied to extraordinary circumstances or pending applications for regular operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private Wireless Services STA limits and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee or applicant in the Private Wireless Services may request STA not to exceed 180 days for new operation or operation beyond existing authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicant seeks waiver to operate as a private mobile radio service provider for a period exceeding 180 days, evidence of frequency coordination is required. Requests for shorter periods do not require coordination and, if granted, will be authorized on a secondary, non-interference basis. See §§1.933(d)(6) and 1.939 for related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible circumstances for STA (Private Wireless)
rubrics_metrics.description: STA may be granted in certain circumstances for Private Wireless Services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circumstances include emergency situations; to permit restoration or relocation of existing facilities to continue communication service; to conduct tests to determine necessary data for applications; for temporary, non-recurring service where a regular authorization is not appropriate; and other extraordinary situations where delay would seriously prejudice the public interest. The nature of the circumstance must be fully described and applications filed at least 10 days prior unless good cause is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary operation while awaiting license — special categories and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules provide several specific temporary-operation allowances pending issuance of licenses or during application pendency, each with specified durations and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: Aircraft Radio Station applicants may operate pending issuance for 90 days with certification on Form 605; Ship Radio station applicants may operate 90 days with Form 605 certification; Industrial/Business pool applicants using an already authorized facility may operate up to 180 days under temporary permit with Form 601 and frequency coordination evidence where required (with power/height limits in Canadian coordination zone); Part 90/Subpart S applicants using existing SMR facility may operate up to 180 days with Form 601 certification provided antenna height limits are met; certain itinerant and private land mobile applicants may operate up to 180 days under conditional permit with frequency coordination evidence; General Mobile Radio Service system license applicants sharing multiple-licensed base stations may operate up to 180 days under Temporary Permit with Form 605.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Notice categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission issues Public Notices in the Wireless Radio Services listing information of public significance in several categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories include: (1) Accepted for filing — acceptance of filings and major amendments; (2) Actions — Commission actions on pending applications previously listed as accepted for filing; (3) Environmental considerations — special environmental considerations required by Part 1; (4) Informative listings — discretional information the Commission believes of public significance (do not create rights to file petitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted-for-filing public notices rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will issue public notices at regular intervals listing applications received in a condition acceptable for filing, or returned for correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any application listed as acceptable for filing and later subject to a major amendment, or returned as defective and resubmitted, shall be listed in a subsequent public notice. Acceptance for filing does not preclude later dismissal as defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications requiring public notice prior to grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories of applications, major modifications, major amendments, and substantial assignment or transfer applications must be placed on Public Notice as accepted for filing prior to grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Wireless Telecommunications Services; Industrial radiopositioning stations with exclusive assignments; aeronautical enroute stations; aeronautical advisory stations; airport control tower stations; aeronautical fixed stations; Alaska public fixed stations (others reserved).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications exempt from public notice prior to grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain filings need not be placed on Public Notice as accepted for filing prior to grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: applications/notifications concerning minor modifications or minor amendments; non-substantial (pro forma) assignments and transfers; consent to involuntary assignment or transfer under section 310(b); applications for licenses under section 319(c); requests for extensions of time to complete construction; requests for STA not to exceed 30 days (no plan to file) or not to exceed 60 days pending/after filing; requests for emergency authorizations under section 308(a); applications for temporary authorization under section 101.31(a); any application for authorization in the Private Wireless Services.

rubrics_metrics.name: General grounds for dismissal of applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may dismiss any Wireless Radio Services application under several circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dismissal may be at the request of the applicant; if application is mutually exclusive and another is selected/granted; for failure to prosecute; if found defective; if requested spectrum is not available; or if untimely filed. Dismissal may be without prejudice (allowing later re-filing) or with prejudice (no acceptance for same purpose for one year), depending on circumstances and part-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal upon applicant request and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request withdrawal or dismissal; treatment (with or without prejudice) depends on timing and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal after being listed as tentatively accepted is considered dismissal without prejudice. If applicant requests dismissal with prejudice, Commission will dismiss with prejudice. If winning bidder requests dismissal of a short-form or long-form application, Commission will dismiss with prejudice and the applicant will be subject to default payments under Subpart Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal for failure to prosecute
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may dismiss applications for failure to prosecute or failure to respond substantially within specified time to official correspondence or requests for additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dismissal may be with prejudice in cases of non-compliance with §1.945. The Commission may dismiss with prejudice for failure to comply with competitive bidding requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective application criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is defective if it fails certain formal or substantive requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defectiveness includes: unsigned or incomplete with respect to required answers, informational showings, or other formal matters; requests an authorization not complying with Commission rules and does not contain a waiver request or, if waiver denied, an alternative fully complying proposal; appropriate filing fee has not been paid; FCC Registration Number (FRN) not provided; or it requests a vanity call sign while the applicant has another vanity call sign application with the same receipt date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal when requested spectrum unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be dismissed when the requested spectrum is unavailable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spectrum unavailability reasons: not allocated for assignment in the specific service requested; previously assigned to another licensee on an exclusive basis or cannot be assigned without causing harmful interference; reasonable efforts to coordinate with foreign administrations yielded unfavorable response anticipating harmful interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal for untimely filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may dismiss without prejudice applications that are premature or late filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes applications filed prior to opening date, after closing date of a filing window, or after the cut-off date for a mutually exclusive application filing group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal for failure to pursue environmental review
rubrics_metrics.description: License applications associated with proposed antenna structures subject to §17.4(c) may be dismissed if pending more than 60 days and awaiting submission of Environmental Assessment or other environmental information, unless applicant shows active pursuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid dismissal, the license applicant must provide updates every 60 days reflecting active pursuit until the requested material is submitted. Otherwise dismissal may occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and prohibitions for agreements to dismiss applications or pleadings
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties entering agreements to resolve mutual exclusivity or to withdraw/dismiss petitions/pleadings (or refraining from filing) must obtain Commission approval and submit specific materials and affidavits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing party must submit request for approval, a copy of any written agreement, and an affidavit certifying no receipt or promise of money/consideration in excess of legitimate and prudent expenses (except bona fide merger agreements); exact nature and amount of any consideration; itemized accounting of expenses sought for reimbursement; and terms of any oral agreement. Within 5 days each remaining party must submit an affidavit certifying no payment will be made in excess of legitimate prudent expenses and terms of oral agreements. Payments in exchange for withdrawing or refraining from filing are prohibited except reimbursement of legitimate/prudent expenses reasonably and directly incurred (not considered payment for refraining). 'Legitimate and prudent expenses' defined; 'other consideration' defined broadly (financial and non-financial). Payments related to withdrawing short-form applications awarded through competitive bidding are subject to §1.2105(c). Affidavits must be executed by individual, partner with personal knowledge, or officer with personal knowledge as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on repetitious or conflicting applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Commission has dismissed with prejudice or denied any license application in the Wireless Radio Services (or revoked a license), the Commission will not consider a like or new application involving the same service/area by substantially the same applicant or related parties for 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an appeal or designation for hearing is pending, a like application by the same applicant/successor/assignee will not be considered until final disposition. While an application is pending, any subsequent inconsistent/conflicting application by or for the benefit of the same applicant or related parties will not be accepted for filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to deny standing and filing deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party in interest may file a petition to deny any application listed in a Public Notice as accepted for filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For auctionable license applications, petitions are governed by §1.2108. For non-auctionable applications subject to petitions under §309(d), petitions must comply with this section and be filed no later than 30 days after the Public Notice listing the application or major amendment as accepted for filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to deny procedure, service, content, and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and substantive requirements for petitions to deny and related pleadings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions and related pleadings must be filed electronically via ULS and reference the file number. Petitioners must serve a copy on the applicant and all interested parties per §1.47. A petition must contain specific allegations of fact sufficient to make a prima facie showing that the petitioner is a party in interest and that grant would be inconsistent with the public interest, convenience and necessity; allegations (except official notice) must be supported by affidavit of person(s) with personal knowledge. Petitions to deny major amendments may raise only matters directly related to the amendment that could not have been raised with the original application (except where petitioner gains standing because of the amendment). Oppositions and replies must be served and factual allegations/denials supported by affidavit; timing governed by §1.45 (non-auctionable) or §1.2108 (auctionable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal and disposition of petitions to deny
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may dismiss petitions that do not comply or if issues become moot or petitioner/attorney fails to appear at settlement conference; Commission will state reasons in dismissal letter/order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is granted while petition(s) are pending, the Commission will dismiss or deny the petition(s) and issue a concise statement of the reason(s) for dismissal/denial disposing of all substantive issues raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: License grant timing and grant-without-hearing criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for grant of licenses: auctionable license grants per §§1.2108–1.2109; non-auctionable applications not subject to competitive bidding will not be granted prior to the 31st day following Public Notice of acceptance unless not subject to §309(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will grant applications without a hearing if: (1) no substantial and material questions of fact exist; (2) applicant is legally, technically, financially, and otherwise qualified; (3) grant would not involve modification, revocation, or non-renewal of any other existing license; (4) grant would not preclude the grant of any mutually exclusive application; and (5) grant would serve the public interest, convenience, and necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial and conditional grants and reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may grant applications in part and/or subject to conditions other than the normal authorizations; when it does so it will inform the applicant of the reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such partial or conditional grants are final unless the Commission revises its action in response to a petition for reconsideration. Petitions for reconsideration must be filed by the applicant within thirty days after the date of the letter or order stating the reasons for the partial or conditional grant, and must reject the partial or conditional grant and return the instrument of authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation for hearing and hearing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission cannot make the findings required for grant without hearing, it will designate the application for hearing and notify the applicant and parties in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders designating applications for hearing will specify matters in issue with particularity. Parties not notified may acquire party status by filing petition for intervention within 30 days after publication in the Federal Register of the hearing issues or substantial amendment thereto. Applicant and parties shall be permitted to participate in hearings conducted by the Commission, the Chief of the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau, or an Administrative Law Judge. Burden of proceeding and proof is upon the applicant, except that burdens for issues presented by petitions to deny or enlarge issues are as determined by the Commission or the Chief of the Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction, coverage, termination, and compliance notification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and obligations regarding construction periods, coverage/substantial service requirements, automatic termination, notification of compliance, and requests for extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction period = time between grant date and required commencement of service/operations (set in service-specific rules). Coverage period = time to meet geographic coverage or substantial service requirements (set in service rules). If licensee fails to commence service/meet obligations by the expiration of the applicable period, authorization terminates automatically on the expiration date. Licensee who commences service or meets obligations must notify the Commission by filing FCC Form 601 within 15 days of expiration of the applicable period; for site-specific authorizations the notification must show to which specific transmitters it applies. Licensees may request to extend a construction or coverage period by filing FCC Form 601.
